paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: The image displays two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating Fleiss Kappa values as a measure of inter-annotator agreement, plotted against two different metrics of sample-level ambiguity. Both charts share the same y-axis, labeled "Fleiss Kappa," which ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, with no visible gridlines. The left chart, titled "Ambiguity Std," has a horizontal axis labeled with four numerical values: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, representing standard deviation levels of ambiguity. The corresponding bars, colored in shades of blue that darken with increasing height, show Fleiss Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 respectively, with the values explicitly labeled above each bar. The right chart, titled "Max Ambiguity," has a horizontal axis labeled with integer values 1, 2, and 3, indicating maximum ambiguity levels. The bars, similarly shaded in blue, correspond to Fleiss Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, also labeled above each bar. Both charts show a general trend of decreasing Fleiss Kappa with increasing ambiguity, with the left chart exhibiting a more pronounced drop between the second and third bars. The bars are arranged in ascending order of the x-axis values, and no legend or additional annotations are present.
